name: volatility_contraction_breakout_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: When ATR(14) on 1-min bars contracts to below the 20th percentile of its session distribution, it signals a volatility squeeze that precedes a directional breakout. This is the intraday equivalent of daily ATR contraction patterns. The mechanism is that low ATR indicates temporary equilibrium between buyers and sellers — once this equilibrium breaks, the move is often sustained because trapped traders on the wrong side need to cover. The edge exists because ATR percentile analysis on 1-min bars is not a standard tool — most traders use ATR as a fixed number for stop-loss sizing, not as a dynamic squeeze indicator. The inefficiency persists because real-time ATR percentile computation requires session-level context that standard charting tools do not provide.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 40 crore INR AND daily_ATR(14)/close > 0.01 (min 1% daily volatility)

indicators.name: ATR_pctile
indicators.params: percentile_rank(ATR_14, all ATR_14 values this session)

conditions: ATR_pctile < 20 within last 5 bars (squeeze recently occurred)
bar_range > ATR_14 * 1.5 (expansion bar — range exceeds recent ATR)
long.confirmation: close > high of squeeze range (new high after the contraction period)

short.confirmation: close < low of squeeze range (new low after the contraction period)

entry.entry_price: market order on expansion bar close

exit.target: 2.0 * ATR_14 (measured from the squeeze range, using pre-squeeze ATR for calibration)
exit.stop_loss: opposite side of squeeze range (if long, stop at squeeze low; if short, stop at squeeze high)
exit.trailing_stop: trail at 1.0 * ATR_14 once profit > 1.5 * ATR_14
exit.signal_exit: exit if ATR_pctile drops back below 20 after initial expansion (failed breakout, re-squeezing)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; size inversely with squeeze range width

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; VIX squeeze + ATR squeeze is a strong setup
filters.time_filter: no entries before 10:00 (need session data for percentile) or after 14:30
filters.volume_filter: expansion bar volume > 2x 20-bar SMA (genuine breakout, not drift)
filters.event_filter: squeeze before an event (RBI, earnings) is a strong setup
other_filters: squeeze must be >= 10 bars (10 min) to be considered genuine compression

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — ATR percentile squeeze is not a standard retail indicator

weaknesses: Not all ATR squeezes resolve with directional breakouts — some simply continue as low-vol drift (no expansion)
The 10-bar minimum squeeze requirement may miss shorter compression patterns that also lead to valid breakouts
Using the squeeze range as stop means the stop distance varies — can be very tight (good) or very wide (bad) depending on the squeeze
prior_art: ATR contraction/expansion: John Carter's TTM Squeeze indicator. Bollinger Band width squeeze is the classic version (Bollinger, 2001). Using ATR percentile rather than absolute ATR is an adaptation from quantile-based analysis. Volatility clustering (GARCH) literature supports the theoretical basis for squeeze→expansion sequences.
notes: Edge math: 0.48 * 70bps - 0.52 * 35bps = 33.6 - 18.2 = 15.4 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 4.4 bps per trade. Positive. One of the better breakout strategies due to the favorable W:L ratio. The 2:1 winner:loser ratio is achievable because squeeze breakouts, when they work, tend to be large moves relative to the tight squeeze range.
